data.name: Ghostdream
data.detailed_description:
"When you die, you normally have only one simple wish - to return and tell them - "Hey, guys - it's OK! No need to feel sad! Cause you know what? It's actually OK on both sides, really." But returning is not easy - the only way would be dreams - "half-dreams" - "ghost-dreams". The problematic part is if you get stuck - you turn into a demon. Hard to say what exactly it is, but we presume it's a painful and useless existence. Better to avoid doing this, really.
My personal "problematic part" is that I am already stuck here. No idea how I'll get out this time..."

On his journey to the "Other Side" Reader (and his "natural companion" Writer) meets various Ghosts and Demons, Holy Spirits and Gods. He also meets Singer, who is neither Ghost, nor Demon. At some point she becomes important to Reader. Realizing this won't stop him though.

The world of Ghostdream should be scary, but it is not - it is just dark. The story should be sad since all the characters are more or less dead, but it is not, because they normally remember nothing, except some minor detail or two (for example the protagonist remembers himself reading a book - this is why they call him Reader. It is his only memory after all).

Ghostdream is a retro-style Point and Click Adventure game with puzzles, exploration and story.

- 55+ entirely animated locations (rooms)
- 10+ characters
- 8 Major Puzzles (no items required, exploration of the whole accessible area is a must) + standard adventure actions (like get here, talk there, press this, press that...)
- 16 000+ words story (fully voiced)
- about 10 hours to beat Ghostdream for the first time.
- 20+ songs OST
- 60 pages art book (with a puzzle guide)

reviews.review:
Note: The Art Book is not missing- you grab it from the Store Page using the link to the "manual" on the right. Yes, it helps a LOT to have this, but the puzzles aren't impossible without it. Just old-school hard.

This is a game to buy if you have very particular tastes. It is a game to avoid if you won't find its weird logic compelling, as without that, its flaws would make it more annoying than charming.

Things some will like:
Surreal Art Style
Unusual Story
Old-school Adventure Game Puzzles

Things some will dislike:
Wordy, reverb-heavy dialogue
Old-school Adventure Game Puzzles (yes, this is a plus or a minus, depending on your taste)
Rather abrupt ending

The art style is an obvious one, either you like it or you don't. The Art book is available on this page as the "manual" in the links to the right, but I recommend care if you decide to check it out- it includes many spoilers, including a section that gives the answers or very strong hints to all of the puzzles.

The story is the part that hooked me, despite being initially drawn in by the art. While, structurally, this could be considered similar to many other adventure games, the details and world were very different than the usual fare. For this reason, I was willing to forgive a great deal.

The puzzles are a mixed bag for someone who doesn't really remember pixel hunting with any fondness. There are two pixel-hunt puzzles, and I would have been much happier with something else, but they serve their purpose well. Most of the others are more about brain power and less about stubbornly looking for a hotspot. I was mildly annoyed that the characters implied I couldn't have known the answer to one (very simple) puzzle without the walkthrough, but that could be considered a nod to the fact that in their world, ours is basically a myth, and thus what is common or easily acquired knowledge here could be esoteric there.

The dialogue... left me in a weird place. I found some of Reader's lines of conversation annoying, but at the same time, they drew me further into the world, in some cases even as I speed-clicked through topics I had seen before. The reverb didn't really bother me, but I know some people find it very annoying. Definitely find a Let's Play video or something and watch a tiny bit of the game to see which camp you fall into. For me, it just corresponded to the pulsing of the scenery- of course the sound is going to be odd. 

The ending... everything important gets dealt with, it's just that there's no epic ending cutscene to help you feel accomplished. There is a mildly entertaining non-epilogue, which served just fine for me, but this is the money brick wall many indie games run into, so I am a bit used to it, I suppose.

All in all, I am pleased that I played it, and pleased to own it, but I definitely do think this is a niche piece, for those of us who like their surreality without a strong horror overlay. YMMV.
